**Finding: compliant (sitting at the fallback) — no redline proposed.**

The planner's `likelyAbsent: true` hint was wrong. The insurance covenant is present as ¶14, physically carried under sec-7 ("Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor"), which is why a section-outline scan missed it — the document's internal paragraph numbering has drifted from its section headings.

What the clause delivers, all binding on Contractor (the counterparty, so the obligation runs in our favor):

| Coverage | Playbook preferred | Document | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workers' comp | As required by law | Statutory amount | Meets preferred |
| CGL | 1M occ / 2M agg | 1M occurrence | Aggregate unstated |
| E&O | 2M | 1M | At fallback |
| Cyber | 5M *if processing Customer Data* | None | Not triggered |
| Certificates | On request | On request + notice of material change | Better than preferred |

The judgment call was cyber. The fallback reads "E&O 1M and cyber 2M," which on a literal reading would fail. But the preferred position expressly conditions cyber on vendors "processing Customer Data," and that predicate isn't satisfied here: there's no Customer Data definition, no hosting or SaaS component, and searches for "personal data" returned nothing. §1(c) puts Contractor at its own facility using its own equipment, with on-site presence only incidental and governed by our security rules, and §8 covers our records through confidentiality instead. So the walk-away trigger never engages, and the missing cyber layer is a conditional sub-element rather than a material failure.

One forward-looking caveat worth flagging to the deal team: this is a task-by-task SOW structure, so the data posture is set later, not by this agreement. If a future Statement of Work moves Contractor into a hosting role or gives it custody of personal data, the cyber gap becomes live and the E&O/CGL-aggregate uplift should be raised at the same time.
